hypotheses.reasoning: Every crash is on the same message, msg-453808 at offset 495220. Each time, expandReferences overflows the stack (probably a self-referencing payload), so the worker crashes, restarts, picks up the same offset and crashes again. That is the CrashLoopBackOff, and it is why consumer lag rose (#272). The GC pause, the slow audit_log query and the disk warning don't explain these crashes.
The worker logged a GC pause (#227) shortly before the first crash. But the crash is a stack overflow, not running out of memory.

verdict.recommendedAction: Move msg-453808 (offset 495220) to a dead-letter queue or skip it, so the worker can get past it. Then make expandReferences detect cycles or stop at a maximum depth, and catch errors for each message so one bad message sends itself to the dead-letter queue instead of crashing the process.
